note: State recreation area on the northeast shore of the Salton Sea, about 30 miles south of Indio on Highway 111, below sea level. The visitor center is next to the Headquarters loop, and the New Camp loop is about 500 m south past Varner Harbor. The sea keeps receding: the harbor is closed to boats, and the water now lies across a wide band of open playa. Summers are extremely hot; October to May is the season. --Claude
summary: parks.ca.gov page (restrictions, fees, rig limits, reservation season), ReserveCalifornia facilities 2043/651/918, OSM and imagery read. Open; Mecca Beach (11700) is closed. flags: WATERFRONT (recommend lakefront -> lakeview; reviewer decides): the stored lakefront was set by applying the drawdown rule (measure to the beach/high-water edge). Current imagery shows the Headquarters west row (around 33.5048,-115.9160) 221-249 m from the Salton Sea water across bare white playa. parks.ca.gov says the sea's water level is decreasing, Varner Harbor is 'closed to vessel access until further notice', and craft must be wheeled or carried 'across the beach directly to the water'. This is not a reservoir that refills each year: the Salton Sea is receding for good, so the old high-water line no longer marks where the water returns. On the default-down rule and the kayak test, it fails as lakefront; the open view across the playa supports lakeview. Proposed evidence: 'HQ hookup row 221-249 m from the Salton Sea water across exposed playa (Esri, 2026-11-27); the sea is receding permanently (parks.ca.gov: Varner Harbor closed to vessels, boats carried across the beach). The drawdown rule is for refilling reservoirs. Lakeview.'
